utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. First, I put on the record -- I put on the record that Mr. Mladic is not present in court. The Chamber was informed that he has reported ill. Mr. Lukic, is there anything you could tell us about the present situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I don't have much information, but I'll tell you what I know. I'll just learned, after 9.00 this morning, that Mr. Mladic had health problems, that he spent the whole day yesterday in Bronovo where he was transported after diagnosed being ill. Today he is in the UN Detention hospital and it should be decided today whether he would be brought back to Bronovo or not, because the doctors have to do their checkups today. I -- it's not heart and it's nothing wrong with the brains. It was reported just that -- it's a stomach -- stomach flu, so... he -- he told me that he feels a bit better than yesterday, and I was able to talk to him thanks to guards who provided Mr. Mladic with a phone, although it's not possible, usually, from that unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, I do see that there's no waiver from Mr. Mladic, which means that we would not proceed. At the same time, the Prosecution has asked for ten more minutes to make submissions on -- on a matter which we started discussing last Friday. Now, of course, that's part of the proceeds as well. So if there's no waiver in itself, unless you specifically tell us that we could proceed with that, and with that only, we would even leave that, and perhaps then we would invite the Prosecution to submit in writing what they may have prepared to present orally. But -- because submissions in writing, of course, can still be continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would accept your latest proposal, to have that in writing then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then the Chamber would like to receive any response -- if -- if at all, because you apply -- you made an application, Prosecution has responded. We have heard questions. If you want to make any further submissions, we would expect that to be there as well today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome or Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps it would be easier for all if we just made our oral submissions tomorrow if they're not going to be heard today. It will be less than ten minutes in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It depends on, of course, the Chamber will most likely have to decide on the matter and the earlier we know what the submissions are, the better we will be able to decide. Now, I've got no idea whether a waiver would be there for tomorrow. Neither would I know whether Mr. Mladic would be back by tomorrow; so, therefore, I suggest that -- but one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber received information, very informal and not binding in any way, that you thought that hearing those submissions on this matter could take place -- could -- could be done today orally. Therefore, we are slightly surprised. But, again, it's no blame whatsoever. I mean, you have the right to express your position in court as you wish. But we wondered whether the very impractical way of written exchange of submissions where, of course, the substance of the matter would be the same; that is, that the Chamber is informed about the positions of the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We also think that we might agree only on this issue, to sit without General Mladic since it's more procedural than substantial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm the guilty one. I should have left my -- I switch it off immediately. I'll switch it off immediately, if I still know how to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Usually it's me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't say that I staged it for this purpose, Mr. Lukic, to make you feel more at ease because that would not be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, yes, we could hear the submissions from the Prosecution, and then we can respond during the day so you have everything today. And I just want to inform you that I asked to visit Mr. Mladic in the UNDU but I was also told that I cannot do that because before the doctors see him first, so that's why I don't have more information otherwise I would be rushing to the UNDU already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know what the rationale behind this rule is, but perhaps better first ask about it than to say anything about it. Under those circumstances we turn into private session to hear further submissions from Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We will not proceed any further today. The Chamber would like to be informed as soon as possible about the expectations as far as the recovery of Mr. Mladic is concerned. The Chamber is pleased to hear that it's not a very serious illness, but at least not related to heart or brains, but to something that most people experience now and then. The last concern, of course, the Chamber has is the witness who is waiting to start his -- giving his testimony. Therefore, Madam Registrar, would you please take care that all relevant information will be shared with the Victims and Witness Section so that the Victims and Witness Section is in a position to keep the witness updated about what he can expect. Any other matter? Not. Then we will adjourn, sine die. We stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.46 a.m.,
